one_line: Scholar-king of the Bahmani Sultanate who fought for the Raichur Doab while cultivating learning and diplomacy.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s to early 40s, medium height, lean but solid build with a deliberate, composed posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, neatly trimmed full beard and moustache, wheatish-olive complexion, sharp dark eyes with slightly heavy lids, thick brows; default expression calm and thoughtful, often with a slight furrow of concentration as if weighing counsel.
appearance.hair: Straight black hair cut short and tidy under a tall, slightly tapering domed turban (kulah) in deep jade green with a narrow gold band at the base and a single small white egret feather tucked on the left side.
appearance.costume: He wears a long, calf-length Persianate robe (qabā) in rich deep-blue cotton-silk with subtle vertical jacquard stripes, tied at the waist with a broad maroon cloth belt; over this a sleeveless, slightly flared over-robe in muted cream with narrow gold woven edging runs down the front and hem; the sleeves of the blue qabā are slim, ending in simple cuffs; trousers are narrow white cotton churidars gathered neatly at the ankles; on his feet are soft brown leather ankle-high shoes with gently upturned toes; he wears a plain steel armguard on his left forearm and a narrow leather-bound book pouch hangs from his belt on the right; jewellery is restrained—a single thin gold ring on his right hand and a simple, flat, round silver pendant on a dark cord just visible at the neckline.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved, single-edged Deccan sword (talwar) with a steel hilt, small disc pommel and a plain leather-wrapped scabbard in dark brown, worn slung from his left hip so the hilt angles forward, which he often rests his hand upon while his other hand holds a small bound manuscript volume.

ref_desc: Taj ud-Din Firuz Shah Bahmani is a mid-40s, wheatish-olive skinned scholar-king with a neat black beard, jade green domed turban, deep-blue striped qabā with cream over-robe, white churidar trousers, brown shoes, a dark brown-sheathed Deccan talwar at his left hip and a small book pouch at his belt.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Taj ud-Din Firuz Shah Bahmani as a dignified late-medieval Deccan sultan: mid-40s, medium height, lean but solid build, wheatish-olive skin, oval face with straight nose, thick brows, sharp dark eyes under slightly heavy lids, and a neatly trimmed full black beard and moustache, his default expression calm and thoughtful with a hint of concentration. His hair is short and black but hidden under a tall, slightly tapering domed turban in rich jade green with a narrow gold band at the base and a single small white egret feather on the left. He wears a long calf-length deep-blue cotton-silk qabā with subtle vertical stripes, tied at the waist by a broad maroon cloth belt, over which sits a sleeveless slightly flared cream over-robe edged with narrow gold trim down the front and hem; slim blue sleeves end in simple cuffs. His trousers are narrow white cotton churidars gathered at the ankles, and he wears soft brown leather ankle-high shoes with gently upturned toes. Show a plain steel armguard on his left forearm and a narrow leather-bound book pouch hanging from his belt on the right, with minimal jewellery—a thin gold ring and a small flat round silver pendant at the neckline. His signature weapon is a single-edged, slightly curved Deccan talwar with steel hilt and small disc pommel, in a plain dark brown leather scabbard slung from his left hip so the hilt angles forward, and in one pose his hand rests lightly on the hilt while the other hand holds a small bound manuscript; use a restrained palette of deep blue, jade green, maroon, cream and brown leather, keeping the design heroic, modest and historically grounded.
